artworks.title: Scylla Watching Minos from the Castle Walls
artworks.description: Scylla watching Minos from the walls — Ovid's princess in love with the besieging king of Crete.

artworks.title: Scylla and Nisus
artworks.description: Scylla and Nisus — the lock of purple hair cut from her father's head to open Megara's gates.

artworks.title: Scylla Rejected by Minos After Destroying Her Father
artworks.description: Scylla rejected by Minos after destroying her city — the betrayal rewarded with exile and metamorphosis.

artworks.title: Scylla et Nisus (Scylla Cutting Her Father's Lock)
artworks.description: Monsiau's Scylla cutting her father's hair — the crime that makes the Ciris myth.

popCulture.title: Metamorphoses
popCulture.creator: Ovid
popCulture.description: Book VIII tells the purple lock — Scylla shears her father's life from his head for Minos, then becomes the ciris bird as he sails away.

popCulture.title: Ciris
popCulture.description: The pseudo-Virgilian epyllion retells the Megarian betrayal — Nisus' lock, Minos' siege, and the girl's metamorphosis.

popCulture.title: Scylla of Megara
popCulture.description: The princess who traded a city for love remains the name for filial betrayal sealed by a single purple hair.
